subject: Follow-up: Support access scope, data residency constraints, and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: June Park <jpark@finwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up: Support access scope, data residency constraints, and next steps

June — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can move toward a scoped trial/POC. I arranged items below by priority so your team can flag anything missing.

1) High-priority requirements we flagged on the call
- Data residency: production inference must keep token-level logs and raw request payloads in us-central region only; no cross-region replication.
- PII handling: Redwood will redact or hash any explicitly-marked PII fields, and we will provide the ability to disable retention for specific customer datasets.
- Support access model: FinWave requires least-privilege support access with break-glass audited events and 2-person approval for any elevated session.

2) Evidence & artifacts we offered
- SOC 2 snapshot (controls map and recent report) — attached (SOC2-snapshot-202706.pdf).
- Example support access matrix showing roles, scope, and break-glass workflow — attached (redwood-support-access-matrix.xlsx).
- Draft residency SLA language for inclusion in procurement — attached (residency-sla-draft.docx).

3) Questions for your security/compliance team (short list)
- For break-glass, do you require on-call approval from two separate FinWave identities, or is an internal ticketing acknowledgement sufficient?
- Are there any encryption-at-rest KMS requirements beyond AWS CMKs (HSM-backed) that we should surface now?
- Expected retention window for logs & traces for the POC (default Redwood is 30 days): is that acceptable or do you need shorter/longer?

4) Proposed next steps
- Rishi to confirm technical controls (RBAC role names, break-glass audit events) and reply with a short matrix by EOD tomorrow.
- FinWave security to confirm break-glass approver flow and residency constraints.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to finalize POC gating criteria.

I left room in the attached spreadsheet to fill in rbac role IDs and escalation contacts — please point me to the ticketing handle or approver emails you want listed.

Best,

Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Support access scope, data residency constraints, and next steps

Thanks, Olga — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with security: 

- Break-glass: we require two approvers but can be one FinWave approver + one on-call from Redwood for the POC. Final production will need two FinWave approvers.
- KMS: HSM-backed CMKs are required for production keys; POC can use AWS CMKs but we need a migration plan.
- Retention: security is okay with 30 days for POC, but will require a configurable purge capability before production go-live.

Also, can you confirm whether support engineers ever see unredacted request payloads by default? We need assurance that PII can be auto-masked and that any unredacted access is logged with the reason and approval.

We can confirm the approver emails — use security@finwave.com as the canonical approver group for now. Can you have Rishi send the RBAC matrix back to me and to security@finwave.com?

Appreciate it,

June Park
Head of Platform Security, FinWave
jpark@finwave.com

June / Olga — following up with concrete answers to the items we discussed. Summary first, details after.

Summary
- Support engineers do NOT get automatic access to unredacted payloads. Default behavior: PII is redacted at ingestion when fields are marked in the mapping you provide. Full payload access requires a break-glass event, two approvers (one FinWave + one Redwood for the POC), and an RBAC session that is time-limited to a single IP. Every break-glass event emits an audit record with approvers, timestamp, justification, and a link to the session recording.
- KMS: POC can use AWS CMKs; production requires HSM-backed CMKs (we integrate with AWS CloudHSM or customer HSMs via KMIP — we can run a short migration runbook).
- Retention: we will enable a configurable retention policy per-customer; for the POC we will set 30 days and provide a manual purge API and UI button; production can be configured to 7/30/90 day tiers per contract.

Details / Implementation notes
- RBAC: roles are scoped to the tenant. Example roles: support_read_only, support_elevated_temp, devops_admin. Elevation path: support_read_only -> request elevation via portal -> two-step approval -> temporary role support_elevated_temp issued for N minutes.
- Break-glass workflow: requestor submits an elevation reason; the first approver (FinWave security group) acknowledges; second approver (Redwood on-call) approves — system requires both to proceed. All actions write to immutable audit logs stored in the US region only.
- Audit artifacts: we will export a chain-of-custody bundle (JSON + signed log) for every elevated session. Sample bundle schema attached as a stub in the spreadsheet.

Attachments in this email: I added a populated copy of the RBAC matrix worksheet and an example audit event payload in the spreadsheet. See tab "BreakGlassEvents".

If this aligns, I can update the residency SLA wording in the doc Olga attached and circulate to procurement. Proposed action: quick 30 min sync Wed or Thu: I can walk security through the RBAC/elevation flow.

- Rishi Malhotra
Principal Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-support-access-matrix.xlsx (updated with RBAC sample, tab: BreakGlassEvents)
